title: Efficient lighting and BEE appliance labels
summary: Replacing inefficient lamps with LED lighting and checking Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) star labels when you buy appliances is a practical first step for Indian households. Savings depend on your hours of use and the unit rate on your electricity bill.
content:
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE), Ministry of Power, runs India's Standards & Labelling programme so buyers can compare appliances. Lighting upgrades should be based on lumens (brightness) and hours of use, not on a claimed universal rupee saving.

How to use this in Hyderabad or elsewhere in India:
1. Note wattage of lamps you still run many hours per day.
2. Choose LED replacements with similar lumens and the correct cap (B22, E27, GU10).
3. Enter your DISCOM energy charge (₹/kWh) from the bill — TSSPDCL or TGNPDCL in Telangana — into EcoTwin. The app will estimate kWh and rupee savings from those inputs only.
4. When replacing a refrigerator, AC, or fan, compare the BEE star label on the nameplate or packaging. EcoTwin does not invent star-rating tables.

Do not treat a photograph of a lamp as proof of wattage or efficacy.
implementation_steps: List fittings used more than about two hours a day
Record current wattage from the lamp or fitting if printed
Buy LED lamps matching lumens and cap type
Enter your bill's ₹/kWh and estimated hours into Compare or Action Planner
If buying a major appliance, read the BEE star label rather than relying on appearance
limitations: Rupee savings cannot be computed without your tariff and hours of use
Older dimmers may not work with every LED
This article does not quote unofficial percentage savings as guaranteed results
source_publisher: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power, Government of India
